mappings.note: The telegram form, priced by the word, with the model answer a condolence wire ('FATHER PASSED AWAY TODAY STOP DEEP CONDOLENCES...'). C-1.3-LO-9 is written around exactly this -- a condolence message in the accepted format, with the register and the length the occasion allows. DEFECT: concept tag reads "Theme of 'Words' Poem".
Khetaram's profession (postal worker) -- a one-word recall too slight for any LO, C-2.2 competency.
Which organisation he works for (India Post) -- recall, C-2.2 competency. LO-31 is reserved for items about what the service DOES for its users.
Where the Somarad Branch Post Office is (Rajasthan) -- the posting that fixes the conditions described in C-2.2-LO-30.
The region he is posted in (the Thar) -- C-2.2-LO-30 names the Thar Desert explicitly.
How he travels (on foot, not by cycle, camel or jeep) -- the hardest of the options, and a working condition, C-2.2-LO-30.

The terrain he crosses (sand dunes) -- a condition of the work, C-2.2-LO-30. DEFECT: the answer runs into 'NODIA' and then into a long passage belonging to a different item ('...merely a postman but a trusted confidant...').

'Human connection over geographical barriers' -- the answer needs the barriers (50 degrees, sandstorms, dunes: LO-30) and the connection they are overcome for (the service reaching isolated people: LO-31). Both cited because the statement joins them.
Write a diary entry AS KHETARAM after a day carrying both good and tragic news. Writing in another's voice from their experience, C-1.2. Not C-1.3-LO-9: that is a condolence message, not a diary.

Write, as a village elder, a formal letter to the Postmaster General commending Khetaram and requesting facilities. Real-life purposeful writing, C-1.3; the chapter's only C-1.3 LO is the condolence message, so competency level.

Analyse two cultural symbols: the torn corner (LO-32, the symbol this chapter's outcome names) and the offering of jaggery (LO-14, a custom of the community's life). Both cited because the question names both.
What is offered for good news (jaggery) -- a village custom, part of the way of life the account records, C-2.1-LO-14.
What the jaggery expresses (great joy) -- the meaning of the custom, C-2.1-LO-14. Not LO-32, which is the opposite pole, the torn envelope.
What tragic news he sometimes carries (a death in the family) -- the content the torn-corner envelope signals, C-2.2-LO-32.
How he handles moments of sorrow (with immense sensitivity) -- what his conduct shows about the work, the second clause of C-2.2-LO-30. Not LO-32: the symbol is not what is asked, his bearing is.
The term for bad news ('Ashubh Samachar') -- the phrase that goes with the torn envelope, C-2.2-LO-32.
The visual clue of bad news (a torn corner) -- the symbol itself, C-2.2-LO-32.

Why he will not carry the torn envelope indoors -- bringing the physical symbol of sorrow in would curse the household. This is the interpretation of the symbol C-2.2-LO-32 asks for, not merely its recognition.
Where he stands to deliver an inauspicious letter (outside the house) -- the practice the symbol dictates, C-2.2-LO-32.
How many times he reads the heartbreaking letter (twice) -- part of the ritual around the torn envelope, C-2.2-LO-32.

WHY he reads it twice -- to be certain of the details before breaking the news. The care is what his dedication shows about the work, C-2.2-LO-30, as against the previous item which only asks how many times.
What he does with the letter afterwards (tears it) -- the destruction of the symbol, C-2.2-LO-32.

His belief that bad news must be destroyed so sorrow does not enter the home -- the interpretation of the torn envelope, C-2.2-LO-32. DEFECT, serious: the stem shows only two of the options and the answer field answers a DIFFERENT question entirely ('Khetaram is a dedicated rural postal worker ... posted at the Somarad Branch Post Office'), so the item cannot be marked as stored.
Describe the geographical challenges he faces daily -- shifting dunes on foot, summer winds, 50 degrees. C-2.2-LO-30's conditions clause in full.

How the Thar climate physically affects him -- battered by sandstorms, covered in dust. C-2.2-LO-30. Not LO-33: the phrase 'walking sandman' appears, but the question asks about the effect, not about the figure.
The role of his uniform and turban -- protective gear against sun and sand rather than only a cultural marker. A condition-of-work item, C-2.2-LO-30.
Who receives his deliveries -- isolated hamlets and border outposts, with money orders and official documents. The reach and the mission, C-2.2-LO-31.
Why he is the only reliable link -- no communication infrastructure, so he carries the news, the paperwork and the money. C-2.2-LO-31's inclusive mission.
The significance of the money orders -- survival funds from relatives working far away, in a famine-prone region. The first clause of C-2.2-LO-31, and the concept tag agrees.
Why the villagers wait at their thresholds -- illiteracy and the anticipation of news. The community's daily life around the postman, C-2.1-LO-14.
How he helps beyond delivery -- reading letters aloud and drafting replies. The postman as scribe, which is the way of life the account records rather than the formal service, C-2.1-LO-14.
What counts as an auspicious message and how he is rewarded -- the wedding invitation and the jaggery. Custom and community, C-2.1-LO-14.

The cultural significance of the jaggery -- sweetness answering good news, and his standing in the community. C-2.1-LO-14. DEFECT: answer trails 'Downloaded from www.pdf.tube PAGE 454 CBSE...'; concept tag reads 'Challenges in the Thar Desert', which belongs to the LO-30 items.

Mapped on the answer, which is the only intact part: he continues working out of financial necessity and a strong sense of duty -- what his persistence shows about the work, C-2.2-LO-30. DEFECT: the stem is the previous question plus its full answer plus page furniture plus a single orphan option (d); the real question and options (a) to (c) are missing.
What protects him from the sandstorms (uniform and turban) -- conditions and equipment, C-2.2-LO-30.
Which season's winds are most treacherous (summer) -- a condition of the work, C-2.2-LO-30.
What official paperwork he carries besides mail (official documents) -- the breadth of what the service delivers, C-2.2-LO-31.
He is described as much more than just a POSTMAN -- the point that the account records a way of life alongside a service, which is C-2.1-LO-14 exactly.

What the term 'walking sandman' SUGGESTS -- reading the metaphor rather than recalling it, with the distractors offering literal and mythical misreadings. C-2.2-LO-33 is the chapter's device-interpretation outcome; its wording says 'in the poem Words' while this figure is from the prose, so cited on substance and flagged.
Whose replies he drafts (the villagers') -- the scribe role again, C-2.1-LO-14.
His service described as SELFLESS, against profitable, effortless and temporary -- a judgement about what his dedication shows, C-2.2-LO-30.

The core message -- unsung heroes overcoming hardship to keep human connection alive in remote places. That is the account read as recording both a service and a way of life, C-2.1-LO-14. Not LO-13, which would require the reportage to be set against the poem 'Words'.

Draft a condolence message to an aunt on her father's death -- C-1.3-LO-9 word for word, and the model answer holds the date, the salutation, the sympathy and the closing. DEFECT: the stem fuses an unrelated recall question ('Who is Khetaram and where does he currently work?') and page furniture in front of the real task.

Study the stamps and say who or what they depict -- Kasturba Gandhi, Kishore Kumar, the festival of Teej. Indian cultural and national heritage, so C-4.2, at competency level because CG-4 has no outcomes in this chapter's frame. Not C-2.1-LO-14: the stamps are not the India Post account.
